Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

The patient was admitted to the Department of Urology with complaints of repeated dizziness. Preoperative echocardiography revealed a variation in the arteries, including an ARSA derived from the initial descending aorta right rear to the LSA, an aberrant left vertebral artery that directly originated from the AA instead of the LSA, and an aberrant right vertebral artery that originated from the RCCA rather than the RSA. Computed tomography angiography confirmed these variances. The patient had no other cardiac or vascular anomalies. Mild stenosis was found in the proximal portion of the left common carotid artery (LCCA), adjacent to its aortic origin. The patient underwent treatment for urolithiasis and was administered aspirin and atorvastatin to prevent potential vascular stenosis. The patient was followed up continuously.

text:
**N20**

The patient was admitted to Urology and treated for urolithiasis, so that is the principal diagnosis. Unspecified urolithiasis indexes to urinary calculus, which falls under N20 (calculus of kidney and ureter).

The vascular anomalies (aberrant right subclavian and vertebral arteries) were found incidentally on preoperative work-up. They would be secondary codes (Q27), not the principal diagnosis.
